text: Experts believe that Artificial General Intelligence, or AGI, may arrive within the next twenty to fifty years. Unlike today's AI, AGI could learn and think like a human across many different tasks. This could bring huge benefits, such as faster medical research and smarter education tools. However, there are also serious risks. AGI might take jobs, spread false information, or even act against human interests if not controlled properly. Some researchers are optimistic and expect AGI soon, while others think it is still far away. Either way, most agree that we must develop it carefully and set clear safety rules before it becomes a reality.
